correctness.rationale: Under two length-m unitary Fourier transforms, non-Nyquist residues contain one order q and the opposite-parity ℓ=|q|,|q|+1 contributions, both strictly nonzero for 0<h<1; their two Gram eigenvalues m(a_q±|b_q|) are strictly positive and phase independent. The Nyquist residue alone mixes q=±L and has eigenvalues 2mw(1±cos(Lδ)), producing determinant ratio sin²(Lδ); aligned rings therefore have rank 4L-1 and half-step full rank 4L. The two varying Nyquist eigenvalues spread away from half-step with fixed sum, so every phase yields weakly larger condition number; determinant optimality is unique modulo longitudes, while condition-number uniqueness is not asserted. New evaluations for L=2,3,4 and two heights independently corroborated the determinant ratio; the algebra establishes every integer L.

value.rationale: Spherical harmonic interpolation across latitude rings is a natural numerical-analysis problem. The exact determinant loss and one-dimensional rank defect diagnose sampling degeneracy, while the optimal staggered offset has a closed-form design rule at a sharp bandwidth, meaningful beyond the already-known qualitative half-step trick.

limitations: Only two symmetric, nonpolar and nonequatorial latitude rings, uniform unweighted samples, degree cutoff L=m/2.
Condition number optimum may be nonunique; proof establishes minimum, not unique minimum.
